tutorial.title: Tutorial Guide
tutorial.pavlov.step.select: Click Pavlov in the scene as actor, then use the target selector to choose the Experimental Dog.
tutorial.pavlov.step.ring: Pause and queue Ring Bell. Disable automatic command stepping for precise timing.
tutorial.pavlov.step.unpause: Step once so the Dog hears the bell before food arrives.
tutorial.pavlov.step.inspect-dog: Click the Experimental Dog in the scene to open its association graph.
tutorial.pavlov.step.pair: Queue Feed after the bell has been heard; do not queue both commands in the same step.
tutorial.pavlov.step.settle: Step once after Feed: the reward creates or reinforces the edge immediately. Inspect prediction error and dopamine expenditure in the graph.
tutorial.pavlov.step.repeat: Wait for food to become inactive, then repeat Ring → Step → Feed → Step until real pairing and reinforcement complete (edge {{weight}}), not command counts.
tutorial.pavlov.step.wait-food: Wait until the food observation disappears before testing, so food-driven salivation cannot be mistaken for learning.
tutorial.pavlov.step.verify: Ring alone without feeding, then step at least 11 times. Completion requires real independent salivation (edge {{weight}}).
tutorial.smart-cat.step.1: Select the Trainer as actor and Billi as target. Observe the cat’s own actions; do not press the button for it.
tutorial.smart-cat.step.2: Pair the button sound with food at least 3 times. Command clicks do not count: wait for the real sound–food pairing objective.
tutorial.smart-cat.step.3: Reward the cat after it actually presses the food button, rewarding at least 2 distinct actions. Repeated feeding cannot replace real action evidence.
tutorial.smart-cat.step.4: Stop sound cues and feeding for at least 10 ticks, then let hunger drive an autonomous food-button press. Verify the autonomous objective; cued responses do not count.
tutorial.gosling.step.1: Select Lorenz as actor and the Gosling as target. Switch to Micro in the experiment notebook (F2 also works): you move Lorenz, not the bird.
tutorial.gosling.step.2: During the critical period, Approach Gosling and step once. Attention and dopamine fix Lorenz as its imprint target. A decoy shown first fixes the wrong target; restart if the window is missed.
tutorial.gosling.step.3: Immediately move Lorenz left using Micro arrows/A or Move Away, then step. Watch the Gosling pursue him itself. If it has already caught up, move farther away before testing.
tutorial.gosling.step.4: Keep stepping: verification requires separation reaching 210, at least 80 of pursuit over 3 movement ticks, and a final gap at most 80. Real objectives count—not sound or approach clicks.
